subject: Post-call recap: next steps and booking the technical deep dive
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 15:08:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap: next steps and booking the technical deep dive

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and a proposed path forward so we can loop in the right teams and lock a technical deep dive: 

Summary from call:
- Primary goal: reduce inference cost for clinical summarization pipelines while keeping 99th pct latency under 400ms.
- Data residency and audit logs are hard requirements (FedRAMP-ish controls later this year).
- Current blocker: procurement needs clear evidence for SOC2 + SSO options; platform team wants an ops runbook.

Proposed next steps:
1) 60–75m technical deep dive (Karthik will lead) to walk model choices, expected latency, and SSO/keys.
2) Loop in Security (evidence/SOC2) and Procurement to outline contract/timing.
3) Share a 1-pager demo agenda + tech checklist before the meeting.

Can you confirm who from Security and Procurement we should include? Below are three windows we have next week — pick one and I’ll send a calendar invite: 
- Tue Nov 17, 10:00–11:15 PT
- Wed Nov 18, 12:30–13:45 PT
- Thu Nov 19, 09:00–10:15 PT

I’ve CC’d Karthik to make sure the deep dive covers the right topics; copying Mina to help with procurement coordination. If those windows don’t work, tell us what does and we’ll adapt.

Agenda (attached): high level demo, technical architecture, SSO/KMS options, SOC2 evidence, next steps.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: redwood-demo-agenda.pdf (1 page)

Thanks for the clear summary and the options. Appreciate you laying out the agenda.

Quick answers:
- Security: Natalie Wong (Natalie.Wong@atlashealth.com) — she owns third-party risk and will need SOC2 artifacts plus a short ops runbook.
- Procurement: Mark D'Souza (mark.dsouza@atlashealth.com) — he’ll own commercial/contract timing.

Availability: Wed Nov 18, 12:30–13:45 PT works best for the team. If you can lock that, I’ll make sure Natalie and Mark are on the invite.

Also, can Karthik call out what telemetry/logging we should show during the demo? Natalie will want to see retention and audit log samples.

Natalie / Mark — nice to e-meet you. Quick intro: I’m Marissa, AE on the account. Karthik is our Senior Sales Engineer who will run the technical deep dive and walk the experiment matrix. Mina will help with procurement pacing and collect the security artifacts you need.

Pre-meeting asks to help make the session productive:
- Natalie: could you confirm the minimum SOC2 artifacts you need (type II report, control matrix, sample logs)? If you prefer, Mina can send a checklist.
- Mark: any contractual guardrails or PO cadence we should be aware of ahead of the conversation?
- Samir: please share any SSO provider details (Okta/AD) and whether Atlas requires customer-managed KMS.

Karthik — can you confirm the run of show below and attach the tech-checklist.md (I’ve attached a draft):
- 12:30–12:40 PT: Quick context & goals (Marissa)
- 12:40–13:10 PT: Architecture, latency/cost profile, KV caching, and SSO/KMS options (Karthik)
- 13:10–13:30 PT: Evidence & retention discussion (Natalie) and procurement timing (Mark)

All — thanks Marissa. Confirmed for Wed Nov 18, 12:30 PT. I’ll bring:
- A short perf/cost baseline for the two model families we discussed (quantized vs fp16).
- Live demo plan: 3 short requests to show tail latency and KV cache behavior.
- Telemetry samples: retention, audit log format, and a sample token-level cost breakdown output.
- SSO/KMS slide: Okta integration steps + options for customer-managed KMS.

I attached a 1-page technical checklist for the session and a short runbook snippet that shows the endpoints we’ll call during the demo. If Natalie needs a sample of audit logs in CSV/JSON, I can paste a sanitized example during the call.
